vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: after weighing the arguments on both sides
used to accept a point before you argue against it
used to introduce a qualification to what you have just said
used to contrast two facts of equal weight in one sentence
in most cases, but not always
used before you concede a point to the other side
how something actually works, as opposed to how it is designed
used to restate something more clearly

paras: This memo is one page because the last one was six and nobody read past the second. It opens with what has not worked, on the principle that the room will remember that part anyway and it is better to hand it over than to have it found.

The engineering pipeline gap has not closed. It is where it was in January, and there is no version of the explanation that is not the same explanation. Granted, we lost the two people who were building it, and that is true, and it does not solve anything. To put it another way: the problem is not that we do not know what to do, it is that we have not staffed it. That is a decision, not an accident, and it can be reversed in one meeting.

What has worked is the first ninety days. Attrition under one year of service has come down eleven points since March, whereas attrition over three years has not moved -- which is what we expected and what we wanted, because the second number was never the problem. By and large the onboarding redesign has done what we said it would do. Having said that, it has landed in three sites out of five, and the two that are missing are the two with the highest turnover. On paper the process is identical everywhere. In practice it is run by whoever has time, and in those two sites nobody has time.

Although the budget is flat, we are opening two sites in the United States this year, which will absorb more of my team than the plan currently shows. To be fair to the plan, nobody knew in January that both openings would fall in the same half. On balance I would move the existing budget rather than ask for more, and I would rather have this argument in July than in November. All things considered, I would rather have this year problem than last year.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- mid-year memo written for this lesson, with all figures invented

choices: Reporting the mid-year results and asking for a budget increase.
Naming one unsolved problem as a decision rather than an accident, and qualifying the successes.
Explaining why the engineering pipeline could not be closed.

items: The memo begins with the results that went well.
It says it opens with what has not worked, on the principle that the room will remember that part anyway.
The writer treats the loss of two people as a sufficient explanation.
The memo says it is true and that it does not solve anything, and calls the real problem a decision rather than an accident.
Attrition over three years of service was not the problem the redesign was aimed at.
The memo says the second number was never the problem.
The onboarding redesign has reached every site.
It says the redesign has landed in three sites out of five, and the two missing have the highest turnover.
The writer prefers to move the existing budget rather than request more.
The memo says on balance I would move the existing budget rather than ask for more.

items.situation: Budget flat, two sites opening anyway. One sentence, one linker.
tips: Although the budget is flat, we are opening two sites this year.

items.situation: One number down, another unchanged, both true. Contrast them.
tips: Attrition under one year is down eleven points, whereas attrition over three years has not moved.
Whereas needs a full clause on both sides.

items.situation: Accept the benchmark objection and then answer it.
tips: Granted, the benchmark lags. The leavers under one year are still on market pay.

items.situation: The rollout worked -- except in two sites. Qualify it.
tips: By and large it landed. Having said that, it has reached three sites out of five.
Having said that goes at the start of the next sentence.

items.situation: On paper one thing, in reality another. Say it.
tips: On paper the process is identical everywhere. In practice it is run by whoever has time.
In practice is the phrase that opens the honest half.

items.situation: Weigh both sides and land on one. One sentence.
tips: On balance, I would move the existing budget rather than ask for more.
On balance signals that you have already done the weighing.

listenings.text: Two minutes, and I will spend the first thirty seconds on what has not gone well, because it is the part you will remember anyway. We said we would close the engineering pipeline gap this year and we have not. It is exactly where it was in January, and I have run out of explanations that are not just the same explanation. Granted, we lost the two people who were building it. That is true and it does not solve anything. What has worked is the first ninety days. Attrition under one year of service has come down eleven points since March, whereas attrition over three years has not moved, which is what we expected and what we wanted. By and large the onboarding redesign has done what we said it would do. Having said that, it has done it in three sites out of five, and the two that are missing are the two that need it most. All things considered, I would rather have this problem than the one we had in January.

She did the thing almost nobody does, which is start with the failure. And I want to be precise about why that works on me, because it is not about honesty and it is not about humility. It is about arithmetic. If somebody spends two minutes on the good news, I have to spend the rest of the meeting working out what they left out, and I am not a generous auditor. If they hand me the bad one in the first thirty seconds, I believe the rest, and we get to spend the time on the decision instead of on the search. The second thing she did was concede one point and refuse to let it do more work than it deserved. Granted, we lost two people. That is true and it does not solve anything. I have watched people spend four minutes on an excuse that good. And the third one, honestly, is that she stopped talking at two minutes. I asked three questions and every one of them was about what to do next. That is a good meeting.
